title.en: nominalisation: turning verbs and adjectives into nouns for academic style

explain.ko: 명사화는 동사나 형용사를 명사로 바꾸어 정보를 압축하는 학술적 표현 방식입니다. 'Prices rose because demand increased'는 'An increase in demand caused prices to rise'로 바뀝니다. 이렇게 하면 주어가 길어지지만 객관적이고 격식 있는 느낌을 줍니다. increase, development, introduction, analysis, failure 같은 명사와 cause, lead to, result in, give rise to 같은 동사를 함께 익혀 두면 좋습니다.
explain.en: Nominalisation turns verbs and adjectives into nouns to compress information in academic style. 'Prices rose because demand increased' becomes 'An increase in demand caused prices to rise'. This makes the subject longer but sounds more objective and formal. It helps to learn nouns such as increase, development, introduction, analysis and failure together with verbs such as cause, lead to, result in and give rise to.

lines.t: This lecture covers nominalisation. Academic writing often uses nouns instead of verbs. For example, instead of 'the government introduced', we write 'the government's introduction'. This makes sentences more compressed and objective.

trans.ko: 이 강의에서는 명사화에 대해 다룹니다. 학술적인 글에서는 동사 대신 명사를 사용하는 경우가 많습니다. 예를 들어 '정부가 도입했다' 대신 '정부의 도입'이라고 씁니다. 이렇게 하면 문장이 더 압축되고 객관적으로 보입니다.

items.passage:
STUDY TIP
Pros and cons of nominalisation
Nominalisation makes sentences concise and objective. But overuse makes writing stiff and abstract. Balance verbs and nouns so readers can follow easily.

trans.ko:
학술 팁
명사화의 장단점
명사화는 문장을 간결하고 객관적으로 만든다. 하지만 지나치면 글이 딱딱하고 추상적으로 변한다. 독자가 쉽게 이해할 수 있도록 동사와 명사를 균형 있게 써야 한다.

task.model: As people crowded into the city, housing prices rose. In nominal form: a sharp increase in the urban population led to a rise in housing prices. The introduction of a new policy partly eased the problem. However, further analysis is needed for long-term improvement.

model_trans.en: As people crowded into the city, housing prices rose. In nominal form: a sharp increase in the urban population led to a rise in housing prices. The introduction of a new policy partly eased the problem. However, further analysis is needed for long-term improvement.
